title: Redox Titrations Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A pressure cooker whistles when the rice is done. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (Chapter 7, Redox Reactions) Diya notices the light pink water her mother uses to wash vegetables slowly fade, and we see how chemists use that same pink as a signal that says stop.

You will see what a titration and a burette are, then run a live titration on the molecule bench: purple permanganate drips into iron(II) in acid, each drop loses its colour as 5 Fe2+ give 5 electrons to one MnO4-, until one extra drop leaves the flask light pink at the end point. Then the three ways to see the end point: permanganate as a self indicator, dichromate with diphenylamine (intense blue), and iodine with starch (blue disappears) using Cu2+ and thiosulphate. We learn the n factor (MnO4- 5, Cr2O7 2- 6, Fe2+ 1, thiosulphate 1) and the law of equivalents, M1n1V1 = M2n2V2 or N1V1 = N2V2, solve a worked example two ways, show the trap of forgetting n, and finish with an original NEET pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 76 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 A signal that says stop

0:47 Live titration: permanganate vs iron(II)
1:19 Three ways to see the end point

2:33 Two signals compared, pause and think
